ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: What is true is that regret happens when we view a large-world problem like a small-world problem. In a small world, where all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known, we can be certain about how much we would have won if only we had picked a different horse in a race or chosen different numbers in the lottery. However, in a large world, where not all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known, we can never truly compare the choices we made with those we didn't make. We can never know what would have happened if we had taken another job, or married another person, or moved to another city because those scenarios don't play out without us. So, when we conjure up regrets about what might have been, we are comparing what we know to what we don't know. What's worse is that, much like the upward social comparisons we make on social media, we torture ourselves with how the realities of our situation stack up against an imagined ideal.

questions.passage: What is true is that regret ①<u>happens</u> when we view a large-world problem like a small-world problem. In a small world, where all choices, consequences, and probabilities are ②<u>known</u>, we can be certain about how much we would have won if only we had picked a different horse in a race or ③<u>choosing</u> different numbers in the lottery. However, in a large world, where not all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known, we can never truly compare the choices we made with ④<u>those</u> we didn't make. We can never know what would have happened if we had taken another job, or married another person, or moved to another city because those scenarios don't play out without us. So, when we conjure up regrets about what might have been, we are comparing what we know to what we don't know. What's worse is that, much like the upward social comparisons we make on social media, we torture ourselves with how the realities of our situation stack up against an imagined ideal.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ choosing → chosen: 'had choosing'은 과거완료에 현재분사를 결합한 오류. 'had chosen'(과거분사)이 올바름. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① happens: 'regret happens when ~'에서 단수 주어 regret에 단수 동사 happens 일치로 올바름
✅ ② known: 'all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known'에서 수동태(be known)로 올바름
❌ ③ choosing → chosen: 'had picked ... or choosing different numbers'이면 과거완료 had와 현재분사가 결합되어 문법 오류. 원문은 'had ... chosen'으로 과거분사가 올바름 ← 정답
✅ ④ those: 'compare the choices we made with those we didn't make'에서 those = the choices(대명사)로 올바름
det.tip: 'had picked ... or chosen'에서 chosen은 picked와 마찬가지로 had에 걸리는 과거분사입니다. 등위접속사 or로 연결된 병렬 구조입니다.

questions.passage: ③<u>what</u> is true is that regret happens when we view a large-world problem like a small-world problem. However, in a large world, where not all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known, we can never ①<u>true</u> compare the choices we made with those we didn't make. We can never know what would have happened if we had taken another job, or ②<u>married</u> another person, or moved to another city because those scenarios don't play out without us. So, when we conjure up regrets about what might have been, we are comparing what we know to what we don't know. What's worse is that, much like the upward social comparisons we make on social media, we torture ourselves with how the realities of our situation stack up against ④<u>an</u> imagined ideal.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① true → truly: 'can never true compare'이면 형용사가 동사를 수식하는 오류. 부사 truly가 올바름. ← 정답
det.analysis:
❌ ① true → truly: 'we can never true compare the choices'이면 형용사 true가 동사 compare를 수식하는 오류. 동사를 수식하려면 부사 truly가 올바름 ← 정답
✅ ② married: 'if we had taken another job, or married another person'에서 had에 걸리는 과거분사로 올바름
✅ ③ what: 'we are comparing what we know to what we don't know'에서 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사로 올바름
✅ ④ an: 'an imagined ideal'에서 imagined는 모음으로 시작하므로 an이 올바름
det.tip: 동사를 수식하는 것은 부사(truly)입니다. 형용사(true)는 명사를 수식하거나 보어 역할을 합니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ what → how: 'we torture ourselves with what the realities ... stack up'이면 what이 주어를 도입하지만 stack up(~에 필적하다)은 자동사구로 목적어가 필요 없음. 'how the realities ... stack up'에서 how(방법/정도)가 올바름. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① certain: 'we can be certain about how much'에서 be certain은 형용사 보어 구문으로 올바름
✅ ② had taken: 'if we had taken another job'에서 가정법 과거완료로 올바름
✅ ③ comparing: 'we are comparing what we know'에서 현재진행형으로 올바름
❌ ④ what → how: 'with what the realities of our situation stack up against an imagined ideal'이면 what이 이끄는 명사절인데, stack up against는 자동사구(~에 필적하다)로 what이 할 역할이 없음. 원문은 'how the realities ... stack up against'로 정도/방식의 부사절이 올바름 ← 정답
det.tip: 'how + S + V' 구조는 방법이나 정도를 나타내는 명사절입니다. 'stack up against'는 '~에 비교되다/필적하다'라는 자동사구입니다.

questions.passage: What is true is that ①<u>regret</u> happens when we view a large-world problem like a small-world problem. In a small world, where all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known, we can be ②<u>doubtful</u> about how much we would have won if only we had picked a different horse in a race or chosen different numbers in the lottery. However, in a large world, where not all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known, we can never truly ③<u>compare</u> the choices we made with those we didn't make. We can never know what would have happened if we had taken another job, or married another person, or moved to another city because those scenarios don't play out without us. So, when we conjure up regrets about what might have been, we are comparing what we know to what we don't know. What's worse is that, much like the upward social comparisons we make on social media, we ④<u>torture</u> ourselves with how the realities of our situation stack up against an imagined ideal.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② doubtful → certain: 작은 세계에서는 모든 선택/결과/확률이 알려져 있어 '의심스러운'이 아니라 '확신하는(certain)' 상태임. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① regret: 'regret happens when we view a large-world problem like a small-world problem'에서 후회가 발생한다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ② doubtful → certain: 'we can be doubtful about how much we would have won'이면 작은 세계에서 결과를 의심한다는 뜻. 그러나 작은 세계에서는 모든 것이 알려져 있으므로 certain(확신하는)이 올바름 ← 정답
✅ ③ compare: 'we can never truly compare the choices'에서 선택을 비교할 수 없다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ torture: 'we torture ourselves with how the realities ... stack up'에서 우리 자신을 괴롭힌다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 작은 세계(small world)는 모든 것이 알려진 세계이므로 확신(certain)할 수 있습니다. doubtful(의심스러운)은 정반대 의미입니다.

questions.passage: What is true is that regret happens when we view a large-world problem like a small-world problem. In a small world, where all choices, consequences, and ①<u>probabilities</u> are known, we can be certain about how much we would have won if only we had picked a different horse in a race or chosen different numbers in the lottery. However, in a large world, where not all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known, we can never truly compare the choices we made with those we didn't make. We can never know what would have happened if we had taken another job, or married another person, or moved to another city because those ②<u>scenarios</u> don't play out without us. So, when we conjure up regrets about what might have been, we are comparing what we know to what we don't know. What's worse is that, much like the upward social comparisons we make on social media, we torture ourselves with how the ③<u>illusions</u> of our situation stack up against an ④<u>imagined</u> ideal.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ illusions → realities: '상황의 환상(illusions)'이 상상의 이상과 비교된다는 것은 문맥에 부적절. 우리 상황의 현실(realities)을 상상의 이상과 대비하며 스스로를 괴롭힌다가 올바른 맥락. ← 정답
det.analysis:
✅ ① probabilities: 'all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known'에서 확률이 알려져 있다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② scenarios: 'those scenarios don't play out without us'에서 시나리오가 우리 없이 전개되지 않는다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ illusions → realities: 'how the illusions of our situation stack up against an imagined ideal'이면 환상과 상상의 이상을 비교하는 것. 그러나 원문은 현실(realities)과 상상의 이상(imagined ideal)의 대비가 핵심 ← 정답
✅ ④ imagined: 'an imagined ideal'에서 상상된 이상이라는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: realities(현실)와 imagined ideal(상상의 이상)의 대비가 이 문장의 핵심입니다. illusions(환상)이면 둘 다 비현실적인 것의 비교가 되어 논지가 무너집니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 큰 세계에서 우리는 내린 선택과 내리지 않은 선택을 진정으로 __________할 수 없다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① compare(비교하다): 'we can never truly compare the choices we made with those we didn't make'에서 선택을 비교할 수 없다는 원문과 일치 ← 정답
❌ ② view(바라보다): 본문에 있지만 'view the choices we made with those'는 의미 부적절. view는 관점으로 보다이지 비교가 아님
❌ ③ torture(괴롭히다): 본문에 있지만 'torture the choices'는 선택을 괴롭힌다는 의미로 부적절
❌ ④ conjure(떠올리다): 본문에 있지만 'conjure the choices we made with those'는 구문상 부적절. conjure up이 구동사
det.tip: 'compare A with B'는 'A와 B를 비교하다'라는 구문입니다. 큰 세계에서는 한 선택과 하지 않은 선택의 결과를 비교할 수 없습니다.

det.korean: 그래서, 우리가 일어났을 수도 있는 일에 대한 후회를 __________할 때, 우리는 아는 것과 모르는 것을 비교하는 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① conjure up(떠올리다): 'when we conjure up regrets about what might have been'에서 후회를 떠올린다는 원문과 일치 ← 정답
❌ ② stack up(비교되다): 본문에 있지만 'stack up regrets'는 후회가 비교된다는 의미로 부적절. stack up은 자동사구
❌ ③ play out(전개되다): 본문에 있지만 'play out regrets'는 후회가 전개된다는 의미로 부자연스러움
❌ ④ make up(구성하다/화해하다): make는 본문에 있지만 'make up regrets'는 후회를 날조한다는 의미로 문맥 부적절
det.tip: 'conjure up'은 '(기억·이미지를) 떠올리다, 불러일으키다'라는 뜻의 구동사입니다.

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① 작은 세계에서는 모든 것이 알려져(known) 있으므로 결과를 알 수 있음. 반대
✅ ② 'we can be certain about how much we would have won if only we had picked a different horse'이므로 작은 세계에서 얼마나 이겼을지 확신 가능 ← 정답
❌ ③ 큰 세계에서는 'not all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known'이므로 모든 확률이 알려져 있지 않음
❌ ④ 후회는 '큰 세계 문제를 작은 세계 문제처럼(like a small-world problem)' 볼 때 발생. '큰 세계처럼'이 아님
det.tip: 작은 세계: 모든 것이 알려져 있어 확신 가능. 큰 세계: 모든 것이 알려져 있지 않아 비교 불가.

det.analysis:
❌ ① 복권/경마는 작은 세계의 예시일 뿐, 확률 계산 방법이 주제가 아님
✅ ② 큰 세계(비교 불가)와 작은 세계(비교 가능)의 구별 → 후회의 본질(아는 것 vs 모르는 것 비교) = 글의 핵심 논지 ← 정답
❌ ③ 소셜 미디어는 비유로만 언급됨. 긍정적 영향도 아님(상향 비교로 괴로움)
❌ ④ 합리적 결정 절차는 본문에 없음. 후회의 인지적 오류를 다루는 글
det.tip: 글의 핵심: 후회 = 큰 세계(불확실)를 작은 세계(확실)처럼 착각하여 발생하는 인지 오류.

ch: 큰 세계와 작은 세계의 구별에서 비롯되는 후회의 본질

questions.passage: What is true is that regret happens when we view a large-world problem like a small-world problem. In a small world, where all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known, we can be certain about how much we would have won if only we had picked a different horse in a race or chosen different numbers in the lottery. However, in a large world, where not all choices, consequences, and probabilities are known, we can never truly compare the choices we made with those we didn't make. We can never know what would have happened if we had taken another job, or married another person, or moved to another city because those scenarios don't play out without us. So, when we conjure up regrets about what might have been, we are comparing what we know to what we don't know. What's worse is that, much like the upward social comparisons we make on social media, we torture ourselves with how the realities of our situation stack up against an imagined ideal.

det.tip: 핵심 구조: 후회 = 큰 세계 문제를 작은 세계처럼 보는 인지적 오류. '아는 것 vs 모르는 것'의 비교가 본질.
